changes.before: Board of Supervisors voted unanimously at its regular meeting on Wednesday, 2026-06-10, to approve a curative amendment. Confirmed directly by the Butler Eagle's meeting report, which quotes Supervisors Phil Wulff, Don Pringle, and Mark Lauer on the record from that meeting.
changes.after: On 2026-06-10, the Board of Supervisors carried a motion declaring the zoning ordinance substantively invalid as to data centers and power generation plant/systems and directing preparation of a resolution for July 8; the July 8 minutes record approval of a data-center curative amendment resolution.
changes.reason: Official minutes distinguish the June motion from the later resolution; the effective legal anchor remains to be verified.

changes.before: Curative amendment approved by the Board of Supervisors on 2026-06-10, halting data center and power-generation-plant-system development for 180 days (Supervisor Phil Wulff: 'the board of supervisors needs to undertake formal action to remedy an exclusionary omission... in the zoning ordinance'). A July 31, 2026 Butler Eagle roundup of Butler County municipalities independently confirms Center Township (along with Adams Township) 'went as far as enacting 180-day moratoriums on data centers and related developments.' Specific resolution/ordinance number and official minutes were not located in sources reviewed.

changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 180-day expiry (~2026-12-07). No data center application had been filed in Center Township as of adoption; the pause was adopted proactively, alongside similar action in neighboring Adams Township, while Center, Summit, Jefferson, Penn, Lancaster, and Forward townships in Butler County all worked on data-center zoning ordinances as of the July 31, 2026 countywide roundup. No news of a permanent ordinance adoption, extension, or repeal specific to Center Township was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
